question: Which of the following is NOT correctly matched? [French administrative centres in India]
options: Pondicherry — Capital of French India; seat of the Governor-General overseeing all French possessions
Chandernagore — Administrative centre for French Bengal, managing trade along the Hooghly River
Mahe — French administrative outpost on the Malabar Coast, governed as part of French India under Pondicherry
Calicut — Established as the French administrative capital for the Malabar Coast, replacing Mahe after 1740
wrong_fact: Calicut was never established as a French administrative capital replacing Mahe. Mahe remained the sole French administrative presence on the Malabar Coast. Calicut (Kozhikode) was a major trade port but never a French administrative centre.
explanation: Pondicherry was the capital of French India. Chandernagore managed French Bengal. Mahe was France's Malabar outpost. Calicut (Kozhikode) was an important trade city, historically associated with the Zamorins and later the British, but was never a French administrative capital or replacement for Mahe.

question: Which of the following is NOT correctly matched? [French administrative policies and their geographic application]
options: Pondicherry — Employed a dual legal system: French civil law for French citizens and customary law for Indian subjects (Tamil/Muslim)
Chandernagore — French administration negotiated with the Nawab of Bengal for trading privileges and maintained a semi-autonomous enclave
Yanam — Small French enclave near the Godavari mouth, administered directly from Pondicherry as a subordinate comptoir
Karikal — Administered jointly with the British East India Company under a revenue-sharing agreement post-1740
wrong_fact: Karikal was NOT administered jointly with the British under any revenue-sharing agreement. Karikal was an exclusively French territory under Pondicherry's administration. There was no such British-French joint administration of Karikal.
explanation: Pondicherry's dual legal system for French citizens and Indian subjects is historically documented. Chandernagore operated with Mughal/Nawab-granted trading rights. Yanam was subordinate to Pondicherry as a small comptoir. However, Karikal was a French-only enclave — there was no revenue-sharing arrangement with the British East India Company.

question: Which of the following is NOT correctly matched? [French administrative policies across different geographic zones of India]
options: Deccan (Hyderabad region) — French administrative influence was exercised indirectly through Bussy's French battalion embedded with the Nizam's court
Northern Circars — Ceded by Nizam Ali Khan to the French (represented by Bussy) as revenue grants (jagirs) to fund French forces in the Deccan
Coromandel Coast — Pondicherry served as the apex administrative authority over Karikal, Yanam and other French comptoirs on this coast
Malabar Coast — Mahe was administered as an independent French presidency separate from and equal in status to Pondicherry
wrong_fact: Mahe was NOT an independent French presidency equal in status to Pondicherry. Mahe was a subordinate comptoir (trading post) administered under the authority of Pondicherry. Pondicherry was the sole presidency-level French administrative capital in India.
explanation: Bussy's embedded forces in Hyderabad as administrative-military presence is well-documented. The Northern Circars (Mustafanagar, Ellore, Rajahmundry, Chicacole) were indeed granted to the French as jagirs by the Nizam. Pondicherry administered the Coromandel Coast comptoirs. However, Mahe was a subordinate outpost under Pondicherry, not an independent presidency.
